Identifier names are ASCII by contract (#56): this #set line is NOT a directive — it renders verbatim and %имя% never becomes a variable. PHP's \w under /u (UCP) read the name, consumed the line and expanded the reference; the fixture is what keeps the three engines on one grammar. validate/set-nonascii-name-is-malformed pins the verdict half.
The same ASCII rule on the reference side: %Имя% is not a variable, so a context entry under that key cannot reach the output.

A CRLF-terminated #set keeps its \r OUT of the value: the grammar's value class excludes the four ECMAScript terminators and the tail eats an optional \r. PCRE's dot-plus-$ used to force the \r INTO the value, so every value on a Windows-authored template ended in a carriage return (#56).
A bare \r ends a line for the anchors, so the #set after it IS a directive: extracted, stripped, expanded. PCRE's /m breaks on \n alone and left the whole line as text (#56).

The value's right edge is a line end: the terminator after X here is an escaped U+2028, so the value is exactly 'X' and the rest of the physical line stays in the body. An engine whose value class admits the separator captures 'X<LS>y' instead (#56).
